::: {.why}
A feature that carries most of the model's weight and has no economic story is usually standing in for something structural, and finding out what is more valuable than the model.
:::

## What you should be able to do tonight

- Identify the features carrying the model's performance and check each against an economic story.
- Name at least one feature that is a proxy for something unintended, and say what.

## Tasks <span class='task-total'>65 min</span>

::: {.task-list}
::: {.task}
<input type="checkbox" class="task-check"> [30 min]{.task-min} Investigate the surprising features: for each, check whether it correlates with liquidity, with market capitalisation, with sector membership or with a data-availability pattern. A feature that is really a size proxy will show up as a size exposure in the portfolio, which you can check directly.
:::
::: {.task}
<input type="checkbox" class="task-check"> [25 min]{.task-min} Check the portfolio rather than the model: report the factor exposures of the winning model's portfolio against your standard exposure set. If a large part of its performance is a known factor, the model has rediscovered something you already had and its marginal value is much smaller than the audit table suggests.
:::
::: {.task}
<input type="checkbox" class="task-check"> [10 min]{.task-min} Write the finding into the milestone whichever way it comes out, including if the answer is that the model is mostly a repackaged momentum exposure.
:::
:::

:::
